culture.title: Contemporary Art at Hamburger Bahnhof
culture.description: A disused railway station the size of an aircraft hangar, filled with Beuys, Warhol and whatever is very current.
culture.bonus: Go into the far hall first and work backwards.

culture.title: The Stasi Museum in Lichtenberg
culture.description: Walk Erich Mielke's preserved offices and the collection of cameras hidden in watering cans, birdhouses and buttons.
culture.bonus: Find the smallest concealed camera in the collection.

culture.title: Nefertiti at the Neues Museum
culture.description: Stand in front of a 3,300-year-old painted bust in a domed room built to hold nothing else.
culture.bonus: Walk the whole Egyptian wing before you go to her.

culture.title: Topography of Terror
culture.description: Walk an outdoor documentation trench along a surviving stretch of Wall, on the ground where the Gestapo headquarters stood.
culture.bonus: Read the outdoor panels end to end before going inside.

culture.title: Modern Berlin at the Berlinische Galerie
culture.description: A big bright hall of the city's own art — Dada, Neue Sachlichkeit, divided-city photography — that most visitors skip entirely.
culture.bonus: Find one work made the year the Wall went up.

culture.title: A Concert at the Konzerthaus
culture.description: A classical evening on Gendarmenmarkt in a Schinkel building rebuilt from ruins, on one of the best squares in Europe.
culture.bonus: Arrive early and walk the square at dusk first.

culture.title: The Philharmonie
culture.description: Hear the Berliner Philharmoniker in Scharoun's vineyard-terraced hall, where no seat is far from the conductor.
culture.bonus: Book a seat behind the orchestra and watch the conductor's face.

culture.title: Opera at the Staatsoper Unter den Linden
culture.description: A full production in the state opera house on the boulevard, restored to its 1740s proportions with modern acoustics hidden inside.
culture.bonus: Dress properly and get a drink at the interval.

social.title: Down in the Vault at Tresor
social.description: Go underground into a former power plant, through the long strobing corridor, into the room that gave Berlin techno its name.
social.bonus: Go down to the basement floor and stay for an hour.

social.title: Karaoke at Monster Ronson's
social.description: Take the main stage in front of a full room, or hide in a private booth. Both are correct.
social.bonus: Take the main stage, not the booth.

social.title: Open-Air Cinema at Freiluftkino Kreuzberg
social.description: Watch a film on a wall in a courtyard under actual trees, with a beer, in the dark, in summer.
social.bonus: Bring a blanket — it gets cold about halfway through.

social.title: Sunday Open Air at about blank
social.description: The garden opens in the afternoon and does not really close, with a crowd that treats Sunday as the main event.
social.bonus: Arrive in daylight, leave in daylight.

social.title: Späti Beers on the Admiralbrücke
social.description: Buy a bottle from a corner shop and sit on the bridge railings in Kreuzberg with everyone else doing exactly the same thing.
social.bonus: Stay until someone brings out a guitar, then leave.

social.title: Techno Boat Party on the Spree
social.description: Four hours on a boat with a sound system, going nowhere in particular past the East Side Gallery.
social.bonus: Be on the top deck when it passes the Oberbaumbrücke.

social.title: Round-the-Table Ping Pong at Dr. Pong
social.description: One table, one bat each, a room full of strangers circling it, and beer. Last one standing wins.
social.bonus: Stay in until you are the last two.

social.title: A Night at Sisyphos
social.description: A former dog-biscuit factory turned permanent festival, with sand, fires, several floors and no sense of time at all.
social.bonus: Find the outdoor stage and stay for sunrise.

foodie.title: Beer Garden at Prater
foodie.description: Drink under chestnut trees in the oldest beer garden in the city, open since 1837, where you carry your own tray.
foodie.bonus: Order a Berliner Weisse with the green syrup and drink it anyway.

foodie.title: The Queue at Mustafas Gemüse Kebap
foodie.description: Stand in the famous line at a Kreuzberg window for a chicken kebab loaded with roasted vegetables and feta.
foodie.bonus: Go at an odd hour and see if the queue is ever actually short.

foodie.title: Natural Wine and Small Plates at Otto
foodie.description: A short, sharp seasonal menu in a stripped-back Prenzlauer Berg room, with a wine list of things you have not heard of.
foodie.bonus: Let them pour you something you cannot pronounce.

foodie.title: Cake at Café Anna Blume
foodie.description: Take the corner table on the Prenzlauer Berg pavement and order the breakfast that arrives on a three-tier cake stand.
foodie.bonus: Order the tiered breakfast for two even if there is one of you.

foodie.title: The Counter at Nobelhart & Schmutzig
foodie.description: Sit at a counter around an open kitchen for a menu built entirely from ingredients grown within reach of the city — no pepper, no lemon, no olive oil.
foodie.bonus: Ask why there is no black pepper and listen to the whole answer.

foodie.title: Cinnamon Rolls at Zeit für Brot
foodie.description: Eat a warm, sticky, pull-apart Zimtschnecke straight from the counter of a bakery that mills its own flour.
foodie.bonus: Get the nut one too and decide which wins.

foodie.title: Pho and Summer Rolls at Monsieur Vuong
foodie.description: A bright red Mitte room with a menu of four dishes that changes weekly and a queue that never quite ends.
foodie.bonus: Order the weekly special without asking what it is.

foodie.title: Brunch at House of Small Wonder
foodie.description: Climb a white spiral staircase into a plant-filled Japanese-Brooklyn breakfast room hidden above a Mitte courtyard.
foodie.bonus: Get there before ten or plan to wait.

adventure.title: Kayak the Spree from Treptower Park
adventure.description: Paddle out past the old harbour cranes and the Molecule Man sculpture standing in the middle of the river.
adventure.bonus: Get close enough to Molecule Man to see the holes.

adventure.title: Night Ride to the Oberbaumbrücke
adventure.description: Cycle the river after dark and cross the double-decker brick bridge with the U-Bahn rattling overhead.
adventure.bonus: Stop in the middle and watch one train go over.

adventure.title: The Ruined Fairground at Spreepark
adventure.description: Walk a guided route through an abandoned GDR amusement park being slowly reclaimed as an art site, fallen dinosaurs and ferris wheel included.

adventure.title: Ride the Berlin Wall Trail
adventure.description: 160 kilometres of cycle path tracing where the Wall stood, through forest, suburbs and surviving watchtowers, over one very long day or two easy ones.
adventure.bonus: Stop at every surviving watchtower you pass.

adventure.title: The Reichstag Dome at Sunset
adventure.description: Spiral up Norman Foster's glass dome above the parliament chamber, free, with the city going pink through the glass.
adventure.bonus: Register online at least a week ahead — walk-ups do not get in.

adventure.title: Hike Grunewald to the Drachenberg
adventure.description: Climb a hill built from the rubble of the bombed city for a full circle of forest and skyline.
adventure.bonus: Take the Drachenberg, not the Teufelsberg, and have it to yourself.

adventure.title: Swim in the Spree at Badeschiff
adventure.description: A swimming pool floating in the river, with a deck full of people and the industrial east bank behind it.
adventure.bonus: Swim a full length without stopping.

adventure.title: Sanssouci and the Potsdam Park
adventure.description: Half an hour by S-Bahn to a hillside of terraced vineyards, follies and a rococo palace built for one king to be alone in.
adventure.bonus: Walk to the Chinese House and the Orangery instead of stopping at the palace.

adventure.title: Climb the Siegessäule
adventure.description: 285 steps up a gold-topped victory column in the middle of a roundabout, for the straightest view down the Tiergarten axis.
adventure.bonus: Count the steps on the way up and check yourself at the top.

adventure.title: A Day at Schlachtensee
adventure.description: Take the S-Bahn southwest to a forest lake where Berliners swim, walk the shore loop and drink beer on the bank.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full shore loop before you get in.

chill.title: Float in the Dark at Liquidrom
chill.description: Lie back in a warm saltwater pool under a domed ceiling while music plays underwater and the lights move overhead.
chill.bonus: Stay in the dome pool for one full track with your ears under.

chill.title: The Peacocks of Pfaueninsel
chill.description: Take a two-minute ferry to a Havel island of white peacocks, meadows and a folly castle built as a ruin on purpose.
chill.bonus: Find a white peacock and wait for it to open.

chill.title: The Waterfall in Viktoriapark
chill.description: Climb a small vineyard-covered hill in Kreuzberg to an artificial waterfall that runs straight down into the neighbourhood.
chill.bonus: Walk up the waterfall side, not the path.

chill.title: The Courtyards of the Hackesche Höfe
chill.description: Walk through eight linked art nouveau courtyards, each one tiled differently, off a street most people never leave.
chill.bonus: Get all the way to the eighth courtyard.

chill.title: Coffee at Bonanza in Kreuzberg
chill.description: Sit with a filter coffee from the roastery that helped start Berlin's third-wave scene and watch the street go by.
chill.bonus: Order a filter, not an espresso drink, and taste it black first.

chill.title: Sunset on the Klunkerkranich Roof
chill.description: Climb to a garden bar built on top of a Neukölln shopping centre car park for the flattest, widest sunset in the city.
chill.bonus: Get there an hour before sunset to actually get a seat.
